A monastery church in Bukovina, in northern Romania, built in 1488 by Stephen the Great, prince of Moldavia. Tradition says it went up in under four months after one of his victories.

Stephen fought the Ottomans, Hungarians and Poles for nearly fifty years and built a church after many battles. Voroneț is famous for what came later. In 1547 its outer walls were covered in frescoes, so that villagers standing outside could see the Bible stories. The western wall shows a huge Last Judgment, with angels, the damned and the peoples of the world, including Turks and Tatars.

The deep blue of its paintings is known as "Voroneț blue". It is one of the painted churches of northern Moldavia, listed together by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site, and remains a working convent.
sum: A monastery church in Bukovina, in northern Romania, built in 1488 by Stephen the Great, prince of Moldavia. Tradition says it went up in under four months after one of his victories.
